intent: The floating panel of a Popover, portalled and positioned beside its trigger or another anchor while the popover is open.
typical_uses: A heading and a description over a few controls
A small form whose changes apply to the control that opened it

dont_use_when.situation: A one-line label for its trigger
A list of actions the user picks from
A read-only preview of what a link points to, shown on hover
A popup centered on the screen that blocks the page

invariants.text: The popup is in the DOM only while the popover is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal, so a closed popover renders nothing.

Without `container`, the popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

The popup has the dialog role and takes its accessible name from the PopoverTitle inside it and its description from the PopoverDescription, through `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`; without a title, pass `aria-label` on PopoverContent.

Unless `initialFocus` says otherwise, opening by press or keyboard moves focus to the first tabbable element inside the popup, or to the popup itself when it holds none or the popover was opened by touch; opening by hover moves no focus.
The popup is a flex column 18rem wide that insets its content by 10px and spaces its direct children 10px apart.
The popup renders no caret pointing at its anchor; there is no prop to add one.
The popup fades, scales and slides from its anchor's side on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` popover.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the default positioning when the trigger sits inside a transformed or filtered container, such as an animated panel
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `positionMethod="fixed"`; absolute positioning resolves against the transformed container instead of the page and misplaces the popup

anti_patterns.dont: Fill the popup with a long article or a wide table
anti_patterns.do_instead: Keep it to a few controls or a short text - popover.module.css fixes the popup at 18rem wide, so wider content overflows or wraps into a tall narrow column; move long content to a Dialog or the page

a11y.by: the primitive's Popover.Popup renders role dialog; popover.test.tsx asserts getByRole('dialog') once the trigger is clicked ("opens on trigger click and renders content with kit classes") and that Escape on it removes it ("closes on Escape")

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; an explicit null renders no popup until a node is passed
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers.

anchor.states: anchor is the element, virtual element, ref or function returning one that the popup is placed against instead of the trigger
anchor.because: `Element | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null) | null` - live DOM nodes, refs and functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the anchor and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

initialFocus.states: initialFocus picks the element focused on open - true for the first tabbable element (the popup itself when opened by touch), false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the opening interaction type
initialFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus picks the element focused on close - true for the trigger or the previously focused element, false for no move, a ref to an element, or a function of the closing interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` - a ref object and a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, instant, transitionStatus). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through popover.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed inside PopoverContent; only its `container` is exposed, as PopoverContent's own prop.
Composed inside PopoverContent; its placement props are exposed on PopoverContent itself.

good.title: A panel placed to the right of its trigger
A panel positioned against another element and portalled into a themed subtree
good.code:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit cell</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent anchor={cellRef} container={themedSectionRef}>
    <PopoverTitle>Cell value</PopoverTitle>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>

bad.title: A popup expected to inherit a theme scoped to a section
bad.why: The popup portals to the document body, outside the section, so it renders with the document root's theme; pass the section, or a node inside it, as `container`.
